newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra sees strong U.S. Losec sales throughout '97.
newsitem.headline: Astra sees strong U.S. Losec sales throughout '97.

text.p: Swedish pharmaceutical company AB Astra said on Wednesday that it expected underlying U.S. sales of its anti-ulcer agent Losec to continue throughout 1997 at the same rate as in the first quarter.
Astra said underlying U.S. Losec sales, or total Losec prescription growth, rose more than 30 percent in the first three months of 1997 against the same period a year ago.
Total U.S. sales of its blockbuster drug through the joint venture Astra Merck rose 24 percent to $515 million.
"The underlying growth is now nearer 30 percent than 40 percent," Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby told Reuters.
"It is reasonable to estimate that it will stay around this level for the full year."
He said Losec, or Prilosec as it is called in the U.S., was now the most sold drug in the U.S..
"We intend to keep this position until the year 2001 when the patent in the U.S. runs out," Ternby said.
Astra Merck is owned 50/50 by Astra and U.S. drugs group Merck & Co.
